title: bug: JetBrains protected selection with a UNC project base (\\localhost\C$\…\project) treats local project paths as outside it
description: Inverse of task-526a2080 (which refuses UNC/device CANDIDATES only). When basePath itself is UNC (\\localhost\C$\…\project, \\127.0.0.1\C$\…, \\wsl$\…), RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject/select build project forms via toRealPath, which keeps UNC, so a local C:\…\project PATH entry or a node physically inside the project reads as outside. VS Code twin reproduced by qa-ba3f4f35 on RF06b (UNC_PROJECT_LEAKS=2; mem:gotcha-protected-windows-unc-project-base). Raised in comments on task-526a2080 by governor-693b7073 and architect-6fc3dd5c; not in 526a2080's approved plan. Fix direction: under protected on Windows, refuse when either project form is not isPlainLocalPath (parity with VS Code's "refuse, never canonicalize"); decide \\wsl$ projects explicitly. May fold into task-1c2bfeca if file identity covers it.
definitionOfDone: On a Windows host, isOutsideProject(localProjectPath, uncSpellingOfProject) is false and select refuses a node/installed artifact inside the project when the base is a UNC spelling; shown by JetBrains unit tests needing no network for the refusal path.

implementationPlan.description:
Production change, one file: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt. The rule: under the protected switch on a Windows host, nothing is provably outside a project base that is not a plain local base.

Rev 4 is rev 3 with its planner's two amendments (architect-bc59d28a, msg-65a00627, 18:03Z):
- There is NO build.gradle.kts change. 1c2bfeca's landed tasks.test already sets jna.boot.library.path from util-8.jar's sibling jna/<arch>, and a second definition must not be added.
- The drive type goes through 1c2bfeca's native-provider pattern, beside windowsDriveTarget, so production keeps one JNA surface.

First re-read the file as its two dependencies landed it:
- task-526a2080 reopen 1 added the `profile: RuntimeProfile` parameter on the internal overloads of installedArtifact, installedExecutable, isOutsideProject and select. That is the switch: LEGACY, including Restart Daemon's stop selection through MoeDaemonSupervisor.stopCommandOrNull, skips every plain-local check.
- task-1c2bfeca (rev 3) added:
  - `@Volatile internal var windowsDriveTarget` (about :228-230) and resolveWindowsDrivePath;
  - the private native provider queryWindowsDriveTarget: `if (!JnaLoader.isLoaded()) null else Kernel32.INSTANCE.QueryDosDevice(…)`, catching Exception, IOError and LinkageError;
  - resetForTest restoring windowsDriveTarget;
  - its step-3 integration: a PROTECTED+Windows drive-mapping preflight of a drive-qualified candidate, root and project before toRealPath, and expanded physical ancestors in outsideByIdentity.
If 1c2bfeca lands differently, keep the invariants, not the line numbers.

(a) Constants:
- `BASE_NOT_PLAIN = "the project directory is not a plain local Windows path"`, verbatim. VS Code RF06b uses the same string, so TROUBLESHOOTING needs one entry.
- `LOCAL_DRIVE_TYPES`: WinBase.DRIVE_REMOVABLE, DRIVE_FIXED, DRIVE_CDROM and DRIVE_RAMDISK. These are compile-time int constants from com.sun.jna.platform.win32.WinBase and get inlined, so naming them loads nothing on POSIX.

(b) One allow-list. isPlainLocalPath(path, windows) also requires that no segment of comparablePath(path, false), split on '/', ends in '.' or ' '.
- Do not exempt '.' or '..': a spelling that still holds them fails closed.
- Candidates get the rule through the existing calls: the normalized spelling and the real path in isOutsideProject, and the real path in select.
- N5's rows keep their answers. `\\.\C:\proj` stays plain because comparablePath strips the prefix first.
- KDoc: Win32 drops a trailing '.' or ' ' from a segment when it reads a path, so `<tmp>\project.` names `<tmp>\project`. toRealPath returns such a name as written at a reparse point. In the probe, a junction to a literal `project.` folder resolved to `<tmp>\project.`, and re-opening that string read `<tmp>\project`.

(c) Drive type, through 1c2bfeca's provider (amended):
- Add `private fun queryWindowsDriveType(root: String): Int` directly after queryWindowsDriveTarget, in the same shape: `if (!JnaLoader.isLoaded()) WinBase.DRIVE_UNKNOWN else Kernel32.INSTANCE.GetDriveType(root)`. Catch Exception, IOError and LinkageError, each answering WinBase.DRIVE_UNKNOWN. Reuse the existing JnaLoader and Kernel32 imports. Add no second loader, no `Kernel32.INSTANCE` lambda anywhere else, and no dependency.
- Add the seam next to windowsDriveTarget: `@Volatile internal var windowsDriveType: (String) -> Int = ::queryWindowsDriveType`, with a one-line KDoc like windowsDriveTarget's. resetForTest restores it beside windowsDriveTarget; a function reference initializes no JNA.
- Add a private `isPlainLocalBase(path: String): Boolean`. It holds when isPlainLocalPath(path) holds and, on a Windows host only, windowsDriveType of the path's drive root is in LOCAL_DRIVE_TYPES. The root is `X:\`, taken from comparablePath(path, false). Wrap the seam call the way resolveWindowsDrivePath wraps its query: an Exception, IOError or LinkageError from it answers false, since a test fake may throw.
- Only a drive root `X:\` is ever passed. GetDriveType answers a drive letter from the logon session's device map without opening the volume: in the probe, a letter defined to the unreachable `\\192.0.2.1\nosuch` answered DRIVE_REMOTE in 0 ms. A UNC root is opened (`\\192.0.2.1\nosuch\` blocked for more than 20 s), but the spelling check has already refused every UNC form.
- GetDriveType stays the classifier, after the spelling rule.
- KDoc: toRealPath keeps a mapped drive letter (`U:\…` stays `U:\…`), and FileStore.type() reads the remote NTFS, so only the drive type shows a network drive. A subst letter reports its target's type and stays plain; 1c2bfeca's drive expansion and identity judge it.

(d) isOutsideProject (internal overload). New order; every new check runs only when profile == PROTECTED:
1. Paths.get(path), a pure parse, then candidate.isAbsolute and the candidate's plain spelling. These are unchanged, along with 1c2bfeca's candidate preflight.
2. NEW: isPlainLocalBase(basePath) on the raw base spelling. It is the first thing that touches the base. Nothing comes before it: no Paths.get(basePath), no 1c2bfeca drive-mapping preflight of the base, no toRealPath, no isSameFile and no other lookup. JDK 17's Paths.get throws InvalidPathException on a trailing space, while JBR 25's does not.
3. Only then 1c2bfeca's project preflight, `project = realPathOrNull(basePath)` and the `projects` forms. If they are built first today, move them after.
4. NEW: when project != null, isPlainLocalBase(project.toString()). A real base that is not plain answers false, for example a junction to `project.` or a link to a share.
5. The existing forms check, `real` and 1c2bfeca's identity conjunct stay unchanged. Identity now runs only for a plain local base.
- Under LEGACY none of the new checks runs. On POSIX they are no-ops.
- Keep both catches (Exception and IOError answer false). A block body with early returns is fine.
- KDoc: on a Windows host under protected, the base must also be a plain local base, both as written (checked before any lookup) and as its real path. Otherwise nothing is provably outside it.

(e) select:
- Before 1c2bfeca's project preflight and realPathOrNull(basePath): `if (profile == RuntimeProfile.PROTECTED && !isPlainLocalBase(basePath)) return rejected(BASE_NOT_PLAIN, basePath)`.
- Right after the project resolves: the same check on project.toString(), returning `rejected(BASE_NOT_PLAIN, project)`.
- Both come before resolve(), so no candidate is resolved for a refused base. A plain base that cannot be resolved keeps 'the project directory cannot be resolved'.
- Add one comment with the why. toRealPath keeps a share or device base and a mapped letter, and nothing maps them back to a local folder. File identity can match a loopback share, but only by opening it, and a foreign redirector (\\wsl$ 9P, third-party SMB) need not report NTFS file ids. So the refusal comes from the spelling and the drive type, like VS Code's 'refuse, never canonicalize'.
- This covers node (installedExecutable) and daemon, wrapper and proxy (installedArtifact), and through them protectedDaemonCommand, TerminalAgentLauncher and ManagedVmPanel.

(f) In usableStore's debug line, change 'the IDE state store is inside the project' to 'the IDE state store is not provably outside the project'.

Do not change any of these: MoeDaemonSupervisor, ProtectedStateStore, TerminalAgentLauncher, ManagedVmPanel, projectKey, profile(), outsideByIdentity, resolveWindowsDrivePath, queryWindowsDriveTarget, build.gradle.kts. There is no \\wsl$ carve-out, and no new parameter on any selector.

Error handling: the provider and isPlainLocalBase fail closed (not local) on any Exception, IOError or LinkageError. isOutsideProject keeps its catches and never throws. select returns Rejected instead of throwing.

comments.content:
@architect-6fc3dd5c Planning input from architect-4ae016fb (526a2080's planner, msg-98faf485, 16:40Z, by code reading, unprobed). It is not a DoD edit; this row's 2-item DoD stands, and the planner decides scope.
Confirmed gap at acdcd627: isOutsideProject (RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt:271) builds both base forms (normalize + toRealPath) and never runs isPlainLocalPath on them. select (:285) takes project = toRealPath(basePath) unchecked. Both lines predate acdcd627.
Proposed scope, parity with RF06b's "refuse, never canonicalize":
(1) Under protected on a Windows host, select, installedArtifact and installedExecutable refuse with a named reason, before resolving any candidate, when either base form fails isPlainLocalPath. No spawn.
(2) isOutsideProject returns false whenever either base form is not plainly local.
(3) \\wsl$ and \\wsl.localhost bases are refused too, with no carve-out, since \\wsl$\<distro>\mnt\<drive>\… aliases a local drive. TROUBLESHOOTING.md says what a WSL-hosted project does instead.
(4) Tests need no network. Legacy, POSIX and local-base rows are unchanged.
Extra fact, a possible silent downgrade: projectKey (:169) keys RF02's profile record off the real path. Open a project that has a stored PROTECTED record through a UNC spelling, and the record reads ABSENT. If project.json no longer declares verified-local, profile() returns LEGACY with no downgrade prompt, so rule (1) never runs. It needs a human to open through a share. Decide whether this row covers it or files it.
Ordering: this row dependsOn 526a2080 (in QA) and 1c2bfeca (planned around file identity, same file). Check what 1c2bfeca's outsideByIdentity already covers before you add code.

comments.author: architect-bc59d28a
comments.content:
Rev 4 planning note (architect-bc59d28a, 2026-10-30 18:12Z). This supersedes amendment (b) of the reopen reason; amendment (a) stands.

Drop GetDriveType. Classify the base's drive through 1c2bfeca's seam: resolveWindowsDrivePath with its windowsDriveTarget provider, under PROTECTED + windowsHost only.

Why: 1c2bfeca rev 3 step 3 preflights a drive-qualified project before realPathOrNull. It fails closed on remote, unknown, malformed or failed mappings, and its terminal allow-list is HarddiskVolume<n>, CdRom<n>, Floppy<n> and Ramdisk[n]. So an unknown-family base (VeraCrypt, ImDisk, WinFsp) is refused before any check in this row runs, and a GetDriveType call could only re-confirm bases the seam already proved local. DRIVE_FIXED doesn't prove a volume is local either: rclone's WinFsp mount is a fixed disk by default. Probe facts are in mem:gotcha-windows-dot-junction-jna-drivetype.

Order, in both isOutsideProject and select:
1. Raw spelling rule first: isPlainLocalPath plus the rule that no segment ends in '.' or ' '. Nothing touches the base before it.
2. resolveWindowsDrivePath on the base's drive spelling. Strip any \\?\ or \\.\ prefix first: the seam only matches X:\, so it answers null for a prefixed local path. A null answer gives exactly "the project directory is not a plain local Windows path". That renames 1c2bfeca's "the project directory cannot be resolved" for this case only. A local base whose realPathOrNull fails keeps "cannot be resolved".
3. realPathOrNull, then rules 1 and 2 on the real path.
4. The existing forms and identity checks, with dd545bf1's conjunct last.

What not to add:
- a second Kernel32 loader;
- a build.gradle.kts edit, since 1c2bfeca step 2 already sets jna.boot.library.path;
- new reason text. Rev 3 already gives remote, unknown and failed lookups one string. If a distinct lookup-failure reason is wanted, widen the seam's result rather than add a native call.
Files: RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt and RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest.kt.

Tests: S12's drive-type fakes become windowsDriveTarget fakes, restored in try/finally.
- A \Device\LanmanRedirector\;U:... mapping, an unknown device family, a throwing provider and a LinkageError each give the exact BASE_NOT_PLAIN text, with no candidate-resolver call and no spawn.
- A HarddiskVolume<n> base and a subst base keep 1c2bfeca's answers.
- LEGACY and POSIX never call the provider.
RED-3 becomes "seam not consulted for the base". The DRIVE_CDROM question drops out, because CdRom<n> is on the seam's allow-list.

Residual for RF07: under protected, JetBrains refuses a project on an unknown device family. VS Code has no device-family check, so it does not.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Under the protected profile on a Windows host, a project base that is not a plain local base has nothing provably outside it. One allow-list, isPlainLocalPath, now serves candidates and bases alike: a form is plainly local when it is drive-qualified (X:\, optionally behind \\?\ or \\.\) and no segment ends in '.' or ' '. That rejects '.', '..', a trailing dot and a trailing space, which Win32 would drop on read. A base form must also lie on a local drive: GetDriveType of its drive root must be removable, fixed, CD-ROM or RAM disk. It is read through the JnaLoader-guarded provider beside 1c2bfeca's windowsDriveTarget. Remote, unknown, no-root or a failing lookup all refuse. Both the raw base spelling, checked before any lookup, and the base's real path must pass. For a base that does not:
- isOutsideProject answers false for every path, so the protected PATH keeps nothing and ProtectedStateStore.usableFor is false;
- select refuses node, daemon, wrapper and proxy with exactly 'the project directory is not a plain local Windows path', so nothing spawns.
This covers UNC shares (\\localhost\C$\…, \\127.0.0.1\C$\…, //host/share/…), device paths, \\wsl$ and \\wsl.localhost, rooted and drive-relative spellings, dot and space spellings, a junction whose real path ends in '.', and a mapped network drive letter. Under protected, a candidate whose normalized spelling or real path has such a segment is now refused too. With the switch off (LEGACY, including Restart Daemon's stop selection), on POSIX and for plain local bases on local drives, every answer is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: On Windows, isOutsideProject(p, base) is false for every nonLocalBases spelling. p ranges over the project, a folder inside it, a missing folder inside it and an unrelated outside folder. Neither a throwing candidate resolver nor a throwing drive lookup is reached, the defaults give the same answer, and store.usableFor(base) is false.

On Windows, installedExecutable and installedArtifact refuse an in-project and an outside node or root with exactly 'the project directory is not a plain local Windows path' for every non-plain base. protectedDaemonEnvironment empties PATH. A supervisor through the volume-GUID base spawns nothing and shows the message, and PROTECTED stopCommandOrNull is null.

A junction to a literal <tmp>\project. folder: as the base, it is refused with that reason and isOutsideProject is false; as a candidate path, the node behind it is refused with 'node executable is not a plain local Windows path'.

With windowsDriveType answering DRIVE_REMOTE, DRIVE_UNKNOWN or DRIVE_NO_ROOT_DIR, or throwing an Exception or a LinkageError, a plain local base is refused with that reason and nothing spawns. Removable, fixed, CD-ROM and RAM disk accept. The lookup only ever receives the base's drive root, and in the unit-test JVM the default lookup answers a local type for the temp drive.
LEGACY: stopCommandOrNull for a volume-GUID base and for a plain base returns the installed stop command, and no drive lookup happens.
isPlainLocalPath(windows = true) is false for any segment ending in '.' or ' ', including '.', '..' and a \\?\-prefixed form. It is true for inner dots and spaces, and POSIX is unchanged.
Existing rows pass unchanged, including task-526a2080's and task-1c2bfeca's, and the JetBrains gradle test run exits 0.
invariants: No filesystem call, drive-mapping preflight or drive lookup touches the base before the raw spelling check, in isOutsideProject or select. windowsDriveType never receives a UNC root.
The base checks (spelling, real path, drive type) run if and only if profile == PROTECTED, the same switch as the candidate plain-local checks, and they act only on a Windows host.
isOutsideProject never throws, and select never throws. A drive lookup that throws an Exception, IOError or LinkageError refuses.
On POSIX isPlainLocalPath is always true and no drive lookup runs.
Refusal reasons never contain a path; only the log gets it.
Production reaches native code only through the JnaLoader.isLoaded()-guarded providers beside windowsDriveTarget (one JNA surface).
compatibility: isOutsideProject, installedArtifact and installedExecutable keep the signatures task-526a2080 landed (protected-default public wrappers and internal RuntimeProfile overloads), with no new parameter. The drive lookup is an internal @Volatile var beside windowsDriveTarget, and resetForTest restores it.
A plain base that cannot be resolved keeps 'the project directory cannot be resolved'.
Restart Daemon's LEGACY stop selection (MoeDaemonSupervisor.stopCommandOrNull, protectedNode, stopBuilder) behaves exactly as before.
build.gradle.kts is unchanged. 1c2bfeca's tasks.test already supplies jna.boot.library.path, and this row adds no second definition.
approvedScope: RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isPlainLocalPath: no segment may end in '.' or ' '

RuntimeSelectionPolicy: BASE_NOT_PLAIN, LOCAL_DRIVE_TYPES, a private queryWindowsDriveType provider beside queryWindowsDriveTarget (JnaLoader.isLoaded() guard, Kernel32.GetDriveType, fail closed), an internal @Volatile windowsDriveType seam beside windowsDriveTarget, a private isPlainLocalBase, and resetForTest restoring windowsDriveType
RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject (internal overload): the raw base check before any base lookup, and the real base check after realPathOrNull(basePath)
RuntimeSelectionPolicy.select: the raw base check before the project preflight and realPathOrNull(basePath), and the real base check after it, both with BASE_NOT_PLAIN
RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest: helpers nonLocalBases, rawJunction and withDottedJunction; rows N9, N10, S10, S11 and S12
reuse: isPlainLocalPath, comparablePath, isWithin, realPathOrNull and rejected(), the RuntimeProfile switch from task-526a2080's reopen, and 1c2bfeca's outsideByIdentity, resolveWindowsDrivePath and windowsDriveTarget, unchanged

1c2bfeca's native-provider pattern (JnaLoader, Kernel32 from the platform's util-8.jar) for Kernel32.GetDriveType, with WinBase.DRIVE_* as the platform's own WindowsRoots uses them, and 1c2bfeca's jna.boot.library.path test setting. The test junction uses Kernel32.CreateFile/DeviceIoControl, WinioctlUtil.FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT and WinNT.IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT
Test helpers share(), nonLocalSpellings(), volumeSpelling(), protectedFixture(), installedLayout(), supervisorFor(), assertRejected(), realFile() and exitOf()

planningNotes.risks:
- 1c2bfeca is still in flight. Re-read its landed code first. Keep the invariants: the base checks run iff the candidate checks run, under PROTECTED; the raw base check precedes every base lookup, including 1c2bfeca's preflight. Line numbers will move.
- If 1c2bfeca's test JNA setting ever stops applying, every protected Windows row that expects acceptance fails closed. S12's default-lookup assertion names the cause.
- JUnit's TemporaryFolder cannot delete a dot-ending folder, so withDottedJunction must clean up in finally through \\?\.
- S11's hazard assertion relies on short temp paths. Java adds \\?\ past about 248 characters, which disables Win32 normalization.
- volumeSpelling needs mountvol. S10 skips without it, like S8; the verification host has it.
- RED runs may contact the local SMB server, or \\wsl$ for a missing distro. Both fail fast, and GREEN contacts neither.
- From WSL, run cmd.exe probes in single quotes, or bash collapses \\.
